content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight run. I built a complete ledger over all 17 claims (three independent: apparatus claim 1, method claim 12, servicing method claim 16), every one of the 30 entries in draft/numerals.md, every numbered and unnumbered part called out in the six figure briefs, the Brief Description of Drawings, and every specific structure, relationship, result, operating condition, and variant in the Summary and Detailed Description, tracing each to an exact affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md (the conversation's single USER passage is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing). The bulk of the text traces cleanly and verbatim: the four bodies; tray feet and the lower return passage; tray side walls spaced inward forming two side supply passages; perforations; the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes and resting above the tray and below the lid; the central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, and peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages; the full passive flow sequence and the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative limitation; the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module to the registered overlap position; the gasket sealing against the upper edge after registration; resilient feet pressed against shell ledges so the module cannot lift; the wick, shallow condensate channel, lower-end condensate discharge openings, and pull tab accessible when the tray is removed; and the whole exposure-indicator chain (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, irreversibility, manual reset after opening, no airflow control). Both optional features are recited as optional, matching "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features." Numeral hygiene checked: all 30 numerals appear in the description and on at least one figure, each denotes exactly one part, and tray feet 22 and resilient feet 54 are kept distinct. Claim antecedents, claim-to-description term parity, statutory classes, absence of means-plus-function language, abstract word count (about 137 words), the "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support sections against input/brief.md, and the single section designation "line 2-2" repeated in FIG-1's brief, FIG-2's brief, and the Brief Description were all checked. The rectangular shell, tray, lid slab, and module outlines stay confined to the figure briefs; the claims and description are shape-neutral, and the application text contains no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language justifying a renderer's choice, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative. Five defects remain. One is critical: FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, stating it is "open toward the bore and open at its outer side" and fixing the axial depth of the stem's outer end "within the housing and short of that outer side" — depth and port relationships the disclosure never states and which the v10 functional-surface rule treats as substantive even in a schematic view. Two are verified internal inconsistencies: FIG-3 asserts the inter-cassette space "communicates with both ducts 48" while describing an upper web continuous across the full width with the ducts outboard of the cassettes, so the described elements leave no path for the disclosed sequence; and FIG-1 shows the lid turned over with its underside toward the viewer while simultaneously stating the gasket is "positioned to face the upper edge 16", the module recess is "directly below the depending indexing rib 62", and the lid "lies above the module 40 on the same upright axis". Two are minor: the Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism ("condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48"), and claim 16 says tray removal is "thereby exposing a pull tab" where the disclosure and description say the tab "remains accessible". Each finding carries a filing-clean fix; no rendered image was inspected.

findings.title: FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, with an outer-side opening and a stated stem depth within it
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, bullet "Mechanical exposure indicator 80"; and figures/FIG-2.md, bullet "Shell side wall 14" ("A small housing, shown schematically, stands proud of the outer face of the left shell side wall 14")
findings.detail: The brief does not merely give the disclosed indicator a generic outline; it assigns the enclosure a technical function and states relationships the inventor never disclosed: that the enclosure is open toward the bore, that it is open at its outer side, that its interior is aligned with the bore, and that the outer end of the stem lies within the enclosure and short of that outer side in the retained condition. Which end of a port is open and how deep a member sits relative to that opening is functional-surface geometry and is substantive even in a view the brief calls schematic. No affirmative USER passage discloses any housing, any outer-side opening, or the axial position of the stem's outer end relative to such an opening. The disclosure discloses only that the indicator is visible from outside, that the stem is thermally coupled to one cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch, and that a spring moves the stem to a latched exposed position; it says nothing about the enclosure that renders it visible or where the stem sits before actuation. The claims and description are correspondingly silent, so this geometry originates only in the figure brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-6.md): "comprising the stem 82, the latch 84, the spring 86 and an unnumbered housing that stands proud of that outer surface, the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the housing is shown schematically as a hatched box of modest size, open toward the bore and open at its outer side, its interior blank and aligned with the bore, the outer end of the stem 82 lying within the housing and short of that outer side in the retained condition shown". Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch. If that cassette softens enough to release the latch, a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position." No affirmative passage anywhere in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage of input/conversation.md discloses a housing, an opening at its outer side, or the depth of the stem's outer end within it.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md replace the "Mechanical exposure indicator 80" bullet with: "Mechanical exposure indicator 80: the indicator assembly at the outer surface of the shell side wall 14, comprising the stem 82, the latch 84 and the spring 86, the assembly shown schematically within an unnumbered plain outline and the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the indicator 80 is shown in the retained condition, the stem 82 not yet having been moved by the spring 86 to the latched exposed position in which it is visible from outside the carrier." Delete the clauses "open toward the bore and open at its outer side, its interior blank and aligned with the bore, the outer end of the stem 82 lying within the housing and short of that outer side in the retained condition shown". In figures/FIG-2.md change "A small housing, shown schematically, stands proud of the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." to "The mechanical exposure indicator is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." No change to the description or claims is required, and no shape or optional embodiment is to be added to the application text.

findings.title: FIG-3 asserts the space between the cassettes communicates with both guide ducts, but the geometry it describes leaves no path
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, bullets "Rigid spacer frame 42", "Phase-change cassette 44", "Downward guide duct 48", and the closing statement
findings.detail: The brief describes the frame as an upper horizontal web continuous with an outboard upright web at each side, i.e. closed across the full width at the top, with the mating channel 52 formed as a recess in that upper web. It then describes the two cassettes as held within the frame facing one another across the blank space directly above the central inlet opening 46, and each duct 48 as lying outboard of a cassette, between the cassette's outboard surface and the nearer outboard web. On those described elements the inter-cassette space is bounded above by the upper web and at each side by a cassette, so it has no opening into either duct. The brief nevertheless asserts open communication and the disclosed flow sequence through it. This is a verified internal inconsistency in the brief itself, and it would drive a drawing in which the disclosed path "divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts" is broken.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "Rigid spacer frame 42: a hatched frame body ... drawn as an upper horizontal web and an outboard upright web at each side of the view, continuous with one another." and "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42" and "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and communicates with both ducts 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48." Source requiring the communication (input/disclosure.md): "Warm air rising from the product region enters the central inlet, divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts, enters the side supply passages".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md amend the "Downward guide duct 48" bullet to read: "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42, each open at its upper end to the blank open space above and between the cassettes 44 and open at its lower end at the bottom of the view." and amend the closing statement to read: "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and is open at its upper part to the upper end of each duct 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48." This states only the open communication that the disclosed flow sequence itself requires and adds no cassette proportion, no contact, and no new function.

findings.title: FIG-1 shows the lid turned over yet states relationships that hold only for an upright, axially aligned lid
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, bullets "Insulated lid 60", "Depending indexing rib 62", "Removable thermal module 40", and the alignment statement
findings.detail: The brief directs that the lid be drawn turned over about its front edge so that its underside faces the viewer, and places the gasket 64 and the rib 62 on that viewer-facing underside. In that attitude the gasket band faces up and forward, not down toward the upper edge 16, and the rib projects toward the viewer rather than downward, so it cannot lie directly above the recess in the module's upper surface. The same bullet set also states that the lid lies above the module on the same upright axis with the parts poised to descend into the shell, which an inverted body cannot do. Three statements in one brief therefore contradict the chosen depiction, leaving the renderer no consistent geometry to draw.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "Insulated lid 60: ... shown turned over about its front edge in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside ... positioned to face the upper edge 16."; "Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view"; "an unnumbered upwardly open recess being formed in its upper surface directly below the depending indexing rib 62"; "The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the lid 60 lies above the module 40 on the same upright axis."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, rewrite the affected wording so the inverted attitude is stated once and every relationship is expressed as a closed-condition relationship: change the lid bullet to "Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab, shown schematically, floating above the module 40, matching the shell 10 in plan, shown inverted in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside, shown schematically as a continuous band running around it in register with the upper edge 16, which it meets when the lid 60 is closed."; change the rib bullet to "Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view, shown schematically, the rib 62 entering the recess in the upper surface of the module 40 when the lid 60 is closed."; in the module bullet replace "directly below the depending indexing rib 62" with "positioned to receive the depending indexing rib 62 when the lid 60 is closed"; and change the alignment statement to "The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the inverted lid 60 is drawn above the module 40 on the same upright axis."

findings.title: Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism inside the guide ducts
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Condensate handling and the removable wick", second sentence
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel, which supports condensate being present in the ducts and reaching their lower ends. It does not state where the condensate forms, and it does not state that the guide ducts have cooled surfaces. The candidate adds both, asserting an operating mechanism (condensation on cooled duct surfaces) that no affirmative USER passage supplies. The assertion also depends on the figure brief's choice that a cassette surface bounds the duct, which is itself only a drawing convention and is not verbalized in the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "Moisture that condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56, rather than collecting on the payload or standing in the bottom of the interior." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray. Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel." There is no passage stating that condensate forms on surfaces within the ducts or that the duct surfaces are cooled.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "Condensate that collects within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56 into the shallow condensate channel 70, rather than standing in the bottom of the interior."

findings.title: Claim 16 says tray removal exposes the pull tab, where the disclosure and description say the tab remains accessible
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 16, third step; compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Condensate handling and the removable wick"
findings.detail: The disclosure and the description both express the relationship as the pull tab remaining accessible once the product tray is removed. Claim 16 recasts it as removal of the tray exposing the tab, which implies the tab was previously concealed and is a different relationship from the one the inventor stated. Claims and description must use the same relationship and the same terms for the same feature.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/09-claims.md, claim 16): "lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, thereby exposing a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel". Source (input/disclosure.md): "A pull tab on the wick remains accessible when the product tray is removed, allowing the wick to be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette." Description (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "The pull tab 74 remains accessible when the removable product tray 20 is removed".
findings.fix: In claim 16 replace "thereby exposing a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray" with "a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel" so the step reads "lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel receiving condensate from condensate discharge openings at lower ends of the downward guide ducts;".

structured_output.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight run. I built a complete ledger over all 17 claims (three independent: apparatus claim 1, method claim 12, servicing method claim 16), every one of the 30 entries in draft/numerals.md, every numbered and unnumbered part called out in the six figure briefs, the Brief Description of Drawings, and every specific structure, relationship, result, operating condition, and variant in the Summary and Detailed Description, tracing each to an exact affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md (the conversation's single USER passage is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing). The bulk of the text traces cleanly and verbatim: the four bodies; tray feet and the lower return passage; tray side walls spaced inward forming two side supply passages; perforations; the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes and resting above the tray and below the lid; the central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, and peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages; the full passive flow sequence and the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative limitation; the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module to the registered overlap position; the gasket sealing against the upper edge after registration; resilient feet pressed against shell ledges so the module cannot lift; the wick, shallow condensate channel, lower-end condensate discharge openings, and pull tab accessible when the tray is removed; and the whole exposure-indicator chain (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, irreversibility, manual reset after opening, no airflow control). Both optional features are recited as optional, matching "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features." Numeral hygiene checked: all 30 numerals appear in the description and on at least one figure, each denotes exactly one part, and tray feet 22 and resilient feet 54 are kept distinct. Claim antecedents, claim-to-description term parity, statutory classes, absence of means-plus-function language, abstract word count (about 137 words), the "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support sections against input/brief.md, and the single section designation "line 2-2" repeated in FIG-1's brief, FIG-2's brief, and the Brief Description were all checked. The rectangular shell, tray, lid slab, and module outlines stay confined to the figure briefs; the claims and description are shape-neutral, and the application text contains no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language justifying a renderer's choice, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative. Five defects remain. One is critical: FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, stating it is "open toward the bore and open at its outer side" and fixing the axial depth of the stem's outer end "within the housing and short of that outer side" — depth and port relationships the disclosure never states and which the v10 functional-surface rule treats as substantive even in a schematic view. Two are verified internal inconsistencies: FIG-3 asserts the inter-cassette space "communicates with both ducts 48" while describing an upper web continuous across the full width with the ducts outboard of the cassettes, so the described elements leave no path for the disclosed sequence; and FIG-1 shows the lid turned over with its underside toward the viewer while simultaneously stating the gasket is "positioned to face the upper edge 16", the module recess is "directly below the depending indexing rib 62", and the lid "lies above the module 40 on the same upright axis". Two are minor: the Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism ("condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48"), and claim 16 says tray removal is "thereby exposing a pull tab" where the disclosure and description say the tab "remains accessible". Each finding carries a filing-clean fix; no rendered image was inspected.

findings.title: FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, with an outer-side opening and a stated stem depth within it
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, bullet "Mechanical exposure indicator 80"; and figures/FIG-2.md, bullet "Shell side wall 14" ("A small housing, shown schematically, stands proud of the outer face of the left shell side wall 14")
findings.detail: The brief does not merely give the disclosed indicator a generic outline; it assigns the enclosure a technical function and states relationships the inventor never disclosed: that the enclosure is open toward the bore, that it is open at its outer side, that its interior is aligned with the bore, and that the outer end of the stem lies within the enclosure and short of that outer side in the retained condition. Which end of a port is open and how deep a member sits relative to that opening is functional-surface geometry and is substantive even in a view the brief calls schematic. No affirmative USER passage discloses any housing, any outer-side opening, or the axial position of the stem's outer end relative to such an opening. The disclosure discloses only that the indicator is visible from outside, that the stem is thermally coupled to one cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch, and that a spring moves the stem to a latched exposed position; it says nothing about the enclosure that renders it visible or where the stem sits before actuation. The claims and description are correspondingly silent, so this geometry originates only in the figure brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-6.md): "comprising the stem 82, the latch 84, the spring 86 and an unnumbered housing that stands proud of that outer surface, the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the housing is shown schematically as a hatched box of modest size, open toward the bore and open at its outer side, its interior blank and aligned with the bore, the outer end of the stem 82 lying within the housing and short of that outer side in the retained condition shown". Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch. If that cassette softens enough to release the latch, a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position." No affirmative passage anywhere in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage of input/conversation.md discloses a housing, an opening at its outer side, or the depth of the stem's outer end within it.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md replace the "Mechanical exposure indicator 80" bullet with: "Mechanical exposure indicator 80: the indicator assembly at the outer surface of the shell side wall 14, comprising the stem 82, the latch 84 and the spring 86, the assembly shown schematically within an unnumbered plain outline and the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the indicator 80 is shown in the retained condition, the stem 82 not yet having been moved by the spring 86 to the latched exposed position in which it is visible from outside the carrier." Delete the clauses "open toward the bore and open at its outer side, its interior blank and aligned with the bore, the outer end of the stem 82 lying within the housing and short of that outer side in the retained condition shown". In figures/FIG-2.md change "A small housing, shown schematically, stands proud of the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." to "The mechanical exposure indicator is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." No change to the description or claims is required, and no shape or optional embodiment is to be added to the application text.

findings.title: FIG-3 asserts the space between the cassettes communicates with both guide ducts, but the geometry it describes leaves no path
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, bullets "Rigid spacer frame 42", "Phase-change cassette 44", "Downward guide duct 48", and the closing statement
findings.detail: The brief describes the frame as an upper horizontal web continuous with an outboard upright web at each side, i.e. closed across the full width at the top, with the mating channel 52 formed as a recess in that upper web. It then describes the two cassettes as held within the frame facing one another across the blank space directly above the central inlet opening 46, and each duct 48 as lying outboard of a cassette, between the cassette's outboard surface and the nearer outboard web. On those described elements the inter-cassette space is bounded above by the upper web and at each side by a cassette, so it has no opening into either duct. The brief nevertheless asserts open communication and the disclosed flow sequence through it. This is a verified internal inconsistency in the brief itself, and it would drive a drawing in which the disclosed path "divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts" is broken.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "Rigid spacer frame 42: a hatched frame body ... drawn as an upper horizontal web and an outboard upright web at each side of the view, continuous with one another." and "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42" and "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and communicates with both ducts 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48." Source requiring the communication (input/disclosure.md): "Warm air rising from the product region enters the central inlet, divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts, enters the side supply passages".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md amend the "Downward guide duct 48" bullet to read: "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42, each open at its upper end to the blank open space above and between the cassettes 44 and open at its lower end at the bottom of the view." and amend the closing statement to read: "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and is open at its upper part to the upper end of each duct 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48." This states only the open communication that the disclosed flow sequence itself requires and adds no cassette proportion, no contact, and no new function.

findings.title: FIG-1 shows the lid turned over yet states relationships that hold only for an upright, axially aligned lid
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, bullets "Insulated lid 60", "Depending indexing rib 62", "Removable thermal module 40", and the alignment statement
findings.detail: The brief directs that the lid be drawn turned over about its front edge so that its underside faces the viewer, and places the gasket 64 and the rib 62 on that viewer-facing underside. In that attitude the gasket band faces up and forward, not down toward the upper edge 16, and the rib projects toward the viewer rather than downward, so it cannot lie directly above the recess in the module's upper surface. The same bullet set also states that the lid lies above the module on the same upright axis with the parts poised to descend into the shell, which an inverted body cannot do. Three statements in one brief therefore contradict the chosen depiction, leaving the renderer no consistent geometry to draw.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "Insulated lid 60: ... shown turned over about its front edge in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside ... positioned to face the upper edge 16."; "Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view"; "an unnumbered upwardly open recess being formed in its upper surface directly below the depending indexing rib 62"; "The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the lid 60 lies above the module 40 on the same upright axis."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, rewrite the affected wording so the inverted attitude is stated once and every relationship is expressed as a closed-condition relationship: change the lid bullet to "Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab, shown schematically, floating above the module 40, matching the shell 10 in plan, shown inverted in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside, shown schematically as a continuous band running around it in register with the upper edge 16, which it meets when the lid 60 is closed."; change the rib bullet to "Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view, shown schematically, the rib 62 entering the recess in the upper surface of the module 40 when the lid 60 is closed."; in the module bullet replace "directly below the depending indexing rib 62" with "positioned to receive the depending indexing rib 62 when the lid 60 is closed"; and change the alignment statement to "The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the inverted lid 60 is drawn above the module 40 on the same upright axis."

findings.title: Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism inside the guide ducts
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Condensate handling and the removable wick", second sentence
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel, which supports condensate being present in the ducts and reaching their lower ends. It does not state where the condensate forms, and it does not state that the guide ducts have cooled surfaces. The candidate adds both, asserting an operating mechanism (condensation on cooled duct surfaces) that no affirmative USER passage supplies. The assertion also depends on the figure brief's choice that a cassette surface bounds the duct, which is itself only a drawing convention and is not verbalized in the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "Moisture that condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56, rather than collecting on the payload or standing in the bottom of the interior." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray. Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel." There is no passage stating that condensate forms on surfaces within the ducts or that the duct surfaces are cooled.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "Condensate that collects within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56 into the shallow condensate channel 70, rather than standing in the bottom of the interior."

findings.title: Claim 16 says tray removal exposes the pull tab, where the disclosure and description say the tab remains accessible
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 16, third step; compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Condensate handling and the removable wick"
findings.detail: The disclosure and the description both express the relationship as the pull tab remaining accessible once the product tray is removed. Claim 16 recasts it as removal of the tray exposing the tab, which implies the tab was previously concealed and is a different relationship from the one the inventor stated. Claims and description must use the same relationship and the same terms for the same feature.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/09-claims.md, claim 16): "lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, thereby exposing a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel". Source (input/disclosure.md): "A pull tab on the wick remains accessible when the product tray is removed, allowing the wick to be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette." Description (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "The pull tab 74 remains accessible when the removable product tray 20 is removed".
findings.fix: In claim 16 replace "thereby exposing a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray" with "a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel" so the step reads "lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel receiving condensate from condensate discharge openings at lower ends of the downward guide ducts;".
